newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICAN EYES ON ENGLISH CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICAN EYES ON ENGLISH CUP FINAL.

text.p: England's domestic Pilkington Cup final at Twickenham on Saturday will be closely monitored in South Africa as they prepare to welcome their first British Lions touring party for 17 years.

Not only do Leicester have six Lions in action dangerously close to their departure on May 17 but their showdown with Sale offers fly-half Joel Stransky an ideal platform to impress the Springbok selectors.

Since kicking South Africa to World Cup victory in 1995, Stransky has lost his place to Henry Honiball but his form since joining Leicester has prompted many to rate him the best overseas signing made by a British club all season.
Stransky, 29, remains available for consideration against the Lions although, if the call does not come, he has been asked to represent South Africa in the Jewish Olympics instead.

A record-equalling crowd of 75,000 for a club match will also be able to judge what effect a gruelling domestic season has had on Lions captain Martin Johnson and team mates such as Austin Healey and Irishman Eric Miller.

All save Neil Back, who missed the opening months through suspension, have been playing virtually continuous top-level rugby since the first fully-professional season in England kicked off in September.

Under former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer, Leicester have been working harder then most to broaden their rugby philosophy and some famous names are struggling to last the pace. Dean Richards and Rory Underwood, two of England's finest, have failed to make Dwyer's final selection, although Richards may well appear as a substitute.

Sale are impressive proof of the motivational power of former All Black and Waikato number eight John Mitchell. In company with his compatriot Simon Mannix, Mitchell has instilled a hard edge into the Manchester-based club who have not been involved in any of the previous 25 Cup finals.

The two sides drew 20-20 in the league last Saturday, a result which reassured Leicester of their place in Europe next season, but Sale insist that Manchester United will not be the only side from the city parading a trophy this weekend.

Leicester - Niall Malone; Craig Joiner, Will Greenwood, Stuart Potter, Leon Lloyd; Joel Stransky, Austin Healey; Eric Miller, Neil Back, John Wells, Matt Poole, Martin Johnson (captain), Darren Garforth, Richard Cockerill, Graham Rowntree.

Sale - Jim Mallinder (captain); David Rees, Jos Baxendell, Adrian Hadley, Tom Beim; Simon Mannix, Dewi Morris; John Mitchell, Dylan O'Grady, Neil Ashurst, Dave Baldwin, Dave Erskine, Andrew Smith, Steve Diamond, Phil Winstanley.
